messages:
meera: Heads-up — I'm drafting the ops playbook for private deployment networking: IPAM + DNS bootstrap + rolling-upgrades choreography. Want to align on customer-managed IP ranges and minimal operator steps before launch.

lucas: SG. can you paste the agenda?

meera: Agenda: 1) IPAM contract (allocate/release/reserve), 2) DNS bootstrap & split-horizon support, 3) upgrade choreography (canary -> staged -> full), 4) preseed for airgapped installs, 5) UX for netops. Meeting tomo 11am PT.

ari: Hot take: customers will demand ability to own A records and CNAMEs for inference endpoints. We should support a DNS mode where we emit desired records and the customer's DNS controller pulls them (pull-based webhook) or we support automated updates with explicit consent. :thinking_face:

sam: +1. For IPAM we should expose a simple HTTP contract so installer (onprem) or operator UI (VPC) can call it. Minimal API: /v1/ipam/allocate {pool_id, cidr_hint} -> {ip, lease_id}. Also need reservation TTL and manual release. Example:

```bash
curl -X POST $IPAM/api/v1/allocate -d '{"pool":"customer-1","hint":"10.0.2.0/24"}'
# -> {"ip":"10.0.2.12","lease":"abc123", "gateway":"10.0.2.1"}
```

julia: For airgapped installs we should support a preseed file that contains ipam leases + DNS mappings. That file must be signed and versioned so upgrades can validate.

meera: Good. On upgrades: recommend a three-stage choreography: canary (1 node / 5% traffic), ripple (batch of nodes per region), final. Each stage must include: drain connections, migrate KV-cache, run smoke evals against a golden prompt set, and automatic rollback on latency/cost/regression alerts.

ari: Add requirement: allow customers to opt for "non-disruptive" mode where we only do blue/green for control-plane changes (longer downtime tolerated for data-plane optimizations). Some enterprise customers will pay for that.

lucas: How do we handle IP collisions during upgrades? If we reassign pods/nics we need deterministic mapping or a phased release so customers' firewall rules don't break. Proposal: prefer allocation stable-ids (lease_id) that can be reattached to new node if within same host-tenant pool.

sam: +1. Also expose a reconciliation endpoint so ops can query leases and force-release stale ones. Add metrics: lease_count, stale_leases, orphaned_dns_records.

opsbot: deploy-bot: created doc -> https://redwood.internal/ops/vpc-ipam-dns-playbook (editable) :white_check_mark:

julia: UX ask: operator console should show a preview diffs of DNS changes before pushing to customer-managed zone, with explicit ack.

meera: Launch criteria draft: - IPAM basic API implemented + unit tests, - DNS bootstrap flow validated with 2 customers (one VPC, one onprem), - Upgrade choreography runbook + simulated dry-run w/ canary traffic, - Preseed signing + installer validation, - Observability: metrics + alerts for ip/dns anomalies.

ari: Priorities: P0 = IPAM API + preseed flow; P1 = DNS automation / preview UI; P2 = advanced upgrade modes (paid add-on).

lucas: Dependencies: installer team (preseed parsing), infra (lease store & metrics), devex (console preview), legal (DNS automation consent). I'll make a dependency board.

sam: Quick question: do we plan to support overlapping CIDR pools (customer-owned) with NAT option? Some customers want to bring 10.0.0.0/8 internally and we NAT at edge.

meera: Yes, add NAT-edge mode as stretch goal. For GA we'll require non-overlapping or pre-configured NAT.

julia: I'll draft the preseed schema and signing flow, push to the doc by EOD.

meera: Thanks. Please drop any customer examples or special compliance asks in the doc. We'll sync tomorrow 11am PT. @opsbot can you create a follow-up task list? :pray:

opsbot: task-bot: created tasks: 1) IPAM API spec, 2) Preseed schema, 3) DNS preview UI mock, 4) Upgrade runbook draft. Assignees TBD.

lucas: perfect. bringing in legal & installer leads to the sync.

sam: adding a tiny todo: include sample smoke eval prompts (latency + hallucination checks) in the upgrade runbook so canary can auto-validate.

meera: Awesome — thanks all.
